method: Each build used the supplied placement and draft vocabulary. The main tests sent one warm-up and nine fresh requests per process. Each request used 4,096 input tokens and up to 256 output tokens. Each workload row gives the median of its three requests.
output_hash: SHA-256 of all output IDs as signed little-endian 32-bit integers. The program compared all IDs and the complete answer between each pair.
eligibility: All release checks and each metric must pass against v0.4.0 on both model files. An improvement cannot offset a loss on another request or metric.

last_four_full_logit_vectors.encoding: SHA-256 of the last four float32 vocabulary vectors. Width -1 is the v0.4.0 eight-token window. Width 0 is the candidate eight-token window. Positive widths use the candidate prompt path with checkpoints.

optional_long_copy_cases.method: Compare output with recorded v0.4.0 requests. The two timing samples are from separate sessions.

fixed_residency_window_trace.expert_storage_measurement: When available, the per-window time serving missing expert data overlaps the GPU wait. It must not be added to the GPU wait.

last_four_full_logit_vectors.encoding: SHA-256 of the last four float32 vocabulary vectors. Width -1 is the v0.4.0 eight-token window. Width 0 is the candidate eight-token window. Positive widths use the candidate prompt path with checkpoints.

optional_long_copy_cases.method: Compare output with recorded v0.4.0 requests. The two timing samples are from separate sessions.

fixed_residency_window_trace.expert_storage_measurement: When available, the per-window time serving missing expert data overlaps the GPU wait. It must not be added to the GPU wait.

mixer_down.note: The comparison checked the exact floating-point result for one to eight positions. The two-position tile reduced elapsed time on a four-position paired mixer from 64.15 to 43.95 microseconds. The four-position tile reduced the eight-position case from 112.95 to 64.80 microseconds.

wide_prompt_q8.implementation: The candidate uses the streamed version with no added workspace and retains the smaller-window product below 64 prompt positions.

attention_heads.decision: The smaller head groups slowed the required eight-position test at position 1,800. The candidate keeps the original head grouping.

grouped_weights.decision: Skipping work for groups of ordinary four-, five-, and six-bit rows slowed several matrix shapes in both orders. The candidate keeps the original group operation.

exact_output_score_intervals.method: Check every original full score before measuring how many vocabulary rows survive the bound. The byte ratios exclude scales and correction overhead beyond the recorded format. They are estimates, not timing results.

short_copy_limits.method: Three streaming repetition prompts per limit. The reference is v0.4.0. Each output token is checked by the target model.

streamed_prompt_formats.time_unit: milliseconds per complete product including prompt layout and any weight packing

chronological_attention.mode: Mode 9 selects every visible block and runs the selected-cell operation. Mode 0 uses the original dense operation in groups of up to eight positions. Modes 1, 2 and 4 give that many query positions to each group of threads. Each sample compares every result bit with mode 9. The two orders are reversed.

memory_budgeted_output_selection.method: Read an indexed prefix of the vocabulary and compute a full dense suffix. Each candidate retains original weight bytes. Each width uses four captured inputs, one all-zero tie and mixed zero columns. A full dense reference checks every bound, every suffix score, every retained prefix score, and every winning score and token. The complete selection is timed in both orders.

timed_exact_output_candidates.method: Each step uses the full vocabulary. Mode zero computes every original score. Modes two and three first read a reduced copy, then compute the original score of every row that can win. Each timing includes the bounds, both selections, and full refinement. The probe keeps the original and reports added bytes. Sample four uses zero activations, which makes all rows tie. GPU times are milliseconds per complete selection.

same_address_gpu_tests.method: Both versions used the same input, output, and rotating weight addresses in one process. Each operation read over 64 MiB across its weight copies.

new_prompt_storage_reads.method: Count process storage reads during one new 4,096-token prompt. Count the actual on-disk bytes of the selected missing experts. Each expert is counted once per layer. The rates use the 2.048-second prompt budget. They assume the recorded placement and weight format.

direct_storage_speed.method: Run the supplied read-only SSD test against the first shard of each model. Read 512 MiB per large block size and queue depth. Direct reads bypass the operating system page cache.

earlier_lossless_weight_checks.method: Use the stored weights of the two model files. Mode zero uses the original 16-bit weights. Six reversible layouts return every weight and tested output bit.

expert_storage.method: Read three 64 KiB blocks from each expert tensor. Compress and recover each block. Keep the smaller of the compressed block and the original. Excludes block metadata.

expert_row_equality.method: Decode 16 distributed rows from each of 512 experts in the three projections of layers 0, 23 and 47. Compare full rows within each projection. Also compare four fixed slices of 32 weights per row at matching offsets.

earlier_verification_with_known_tokens.method: Supply the known continuation from the reference answer. Time only verification of the next 255 tokens. The test omits draft generation and ordinary response delivery.

shorter_history_matches.method: Replay each model's nine recorded answers one token at a time. Only the input and tokens already generated can propose a continuation. Count opportunities missed by the eight-token suffix. Score proposals with the remaining release answers.
